decisions.reason: The product has a clear positive signal from its 2019 award and fits the firm's materials and system-solution capabilities, so a large firm would keep this option open while downside carrying cost appears limited.

This is a close adjacency to the firm's tube and energy-system competencies, and with no clear evidence of failure a large incumbent would usually continue the option while market adoption in geothermal applications further resolves.

As a complementary geothermal technology, its standalone success is still uncertain, but the cost of retaining it is likely lower than the value of preserving flexibility in a potentially growing application field.

A fire-protection steel profile system is strongly aligned with the firm's established construction business, and in a growing industry management would be inclined to keep such a strategically coherent option unless results were clearly poor.
The slim steel profile system appears to be a core product-line extension with good fit to customer-specific building solutions, so the firm would likely retain it while learning more about demand.

This decorative surface offering is somewhat more optional and easier to prune than the others, but because it is a low-distance extension of the existing profile business the firm would still more likely keep it than drop it.
